# Run units and timezone probes in one prepared CI job

## Context

Under #20328, the operator asked whether several tasks can share one runner instead of consuming one org slot per shard. The measured exploration is [here](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/20328#issuecomment-6662759491). This first slice consolidates the browserless unit family; it does not change component or E2E execution.

At Engine dev `83006c9747c552ed0e4e0a496049f46211f9247a`, `test.yml` creates one main-unit job and two timezone jobs. In [run 42048502578](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42048502578), main units took 146s; the +14 and −11 probes took 3s and 4s, each after its own 9s dependency install and 11s bundle step. This is a one-run baseline, not a promised speedup.

## The Problem

Three separate runner allocations repeat preparation for seven seconds of additional timezone work. The org queue makes those short jobs wait behind larger jobs. Dropping either timezone is not acceptable: #19005 establishes why UTC alone cannot catch the relevant regressions.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` owns the matrix and dispatch probe interface.
- `playwright.config.unit.mjs` already uses four workers in CI; the timezone config launches a separate Node process and sets `TZ` from `NEO_UNIT_TZ`.
- The current jobs share `/tmp/test-run.log`, a unit JSON reporter path, and (for both timezone probes) an output directory. Even sequential consolidation must preserve each result before the next invocation writes.
- The live dev ruleset requires `unit`, not the two `unit-tz (...)` contexts individually.

Design authority: #20328's terminal predicate says “the fixed checks run as a handful of jobs, not dozens”; the operator requested this aggregation exploration. Preserve #19005's non-UTC falsifiers and the current classifier as scope authority.

## The Fix

Run main units and both timezone probes in one prepared `unit` job. Keep them as separate, sequential processes: main units retain their four-worker policy, followed by +14 and −11 probes. Seven seconds of sampled probe work does not justify another layer of concurrent processes.

Share checkout, Node setup, installation and browser-dependency bundling. Keep one aggregate conclusion that fails for any failed invocation, while reporting all three outcomes. Isolate logs, JSON and failure artifacts. Preserve job-level scope skipping, stale-head protection and the existing dispatch semantics.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback / failure | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Required `unit` context | Current dev ruleset and #20328 | One job covers main, +14 and −11 on ordinary selected runs | Any invocation failure fails the job; canceled or unexecuted work is not success | Forced failure in each position |
| Timezone probes | #19005 and current timezone config | Both signs execute in separate processes without changing the main unit timezone | One failure does not hide the other result | Existing mutation controls and distinct reports |
| Dispatch `suite/specs/repeatEach` | Existing `test.yml` interface | `unit` selects main only, `unit-tz` selects both probes, empty preserves ordinary selection | Existing argument validation and measured-denominator reporting remain | Focused dispatch-selection controls |
| Classifier and current-head gates | `classify-test-scope.yml` | Preserve `run_unit`, full dev selection and stale-head refusal | Skipped work is explicitly reported, not silently omitted | Selected, skipped and stale controls |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Ordinary selected CI runs allocate one unit-family runner job instead of three, preserving the `unit` check name and all three populations.
- [ ] Main, +14 and −11 results, logs and artifacts remain distinct; each timezone is set only for its own process.
- [ ] A controlled failure in any of the three invocations fails the aggregate, while the other selected invocations still produce their results; cancellation/unexecuted cases cannot produce a false green.
- [ ] Classifier skips, current-head checks, full dev coverage and dispatch `suite/specs/repeatEach` behavior retain focused positive/negative controls.
- [ ] Record the candidate's hosted runner-job count, test-step duration, total job duration and coverage against the cited baseline. No reduced test population, relaxed timeout or added retry substitutes for consolidation.

## Out of Scope

Component/E2E worker counts or packing; native parallel-step rollout; the shared baseline (#281 in Skills); Julia's #20344/#20345 surfaces; ruleset changes; timezone production-code changes.

## Avoided Traps

- A new matrix still allocates multiple runners.
- Parallelizing the main four-worker pool with other CPU-heavy suites can add contention; this slice does not do that.
- Reusing report paths erases an earlier failure.
- A combined job must retain all outcomes rather than stopping after the first red.
